A helicopter will be used on a windless (0-10 miles per hour) day so that there will be little if any drift of the spray. Spraying will be done beginning at 5:00 a.m. If wind reaches 7 miles per hour a check will be made of the direction of the spray to assure that it is being sprayed in the right location. If wind reaches 10 miles per hour, spraying will not be continued.
A helicopter has the advantage of low altitude flying which will allow more precise control of the chemical, thus reducing environmental impacts, a more efficient use of the herbicide, and less hazard to the aircraft and its operator.
VIII. Consultation and Coordination
The United States Environmental Protection Agency has advised that the 2,4D herbicide proposed use is registered for the control of wild hemp and can be used on ditch banks as well as other infested acreage. They advised that the program will have no serious impact on the environment.
The Cooperative Extension Service, State of Indiana, Purdue University advised that the program, under the control of one agency far outweighs large indiscriminate individual herbicide application. The Extension Service also advised that the use of granulars eliminates the danger of spray mist settling into the drainage ditches or damaging crops.
Professor Knake of the Agronomy Department, University of Illinois, suggests that precautions should be taken to avoid or at least minimize the possibility of 2,4D getting into the drainage ditches. He advised that the firm selected to spray the fields has done work previously for the Chicago Metropolitan Sanitary District and the work of this company was well accepted.
